question: Indicate which of the following deficits leads to a glycogenosis:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Glucose 6-phosphatase deficiency" -> "inability to convert glucose 6-phosphate to glucose" -> "accumulation of glycogen" -> "glycogenosis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Hexokinase deficiency" -> "impaired phosphorylation of glucose" -> "reduced glucose utilization" -> "possible glycogen accumulation" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency" -> "inability to convert fructose 1,6-bisphosphate to fructose 6-phosphate" -> "altered gluconeogenesis" -> "possible glycogen accumulation" -> 65%
CHAIN: "Hexosaminidase deficiency" -> "impaired breakdown of GM2 gangliosides" -> "not directly related to glycogen metabolism" -> "no glycogenosis" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Fructokinase deficiency" -> "inability to phosphorylate fructose" -> "fructose accumulation" -> "not directly related to glycogen metabolism" -> "no glycogenosis" -> 10%
analysis: Glycogenosis refers to a group of inherited disorders that result in the abnormal metabolism of glycogen. A deficiency in glucose 6-phosphatase leads to von Gierke disease, which is a type of glycogen storage disease characterized by the accumulation of glycogen in the liver and kidneys due to the inability to convert glucose 6-phosphate to glucose. This results in hypoglycemia and other metabolic issues. Therefore, the correct answer is glucose 6-phosphatase.
